summary.headline: Rossari Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 697.2 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.6% from 12.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 697.2 crore (up 28% YoY) and EBITDA hit a record Rs 80.6 crore (up 18.7%), though margin fell to 11.6% from 12.5%. Core B2B EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (up 13%, ~14% margin), with the institutional and B2C businesses dragging margins and remaining flat in growth. PAT was Rs 35.1 crore (up 4.5%). Management is pursuing non-core asset monetisation, B2C exits and product-mix changes, and says Rs 11.6% is the margin base; target is ~15% EBITDA margin in about two years. Raw material spikes, phenol losses of about Rs 5 crore and freight volatility weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: HPPC
segments.commentary: Crossed Rs 550 crore quarterly revenue, growing ~28% YoY; new products such as NMMO, MDEA, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants and fibre finishes are contributing.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals (TSC)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; new Fibre Chemicals Division launched during the quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health and Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; vitamin premix plant now operational; trace minerals and enzyme premixes added. Pharma revenue was above Rs 50 crore last year and is guided to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Growth flat YoY; losses moderated. Institutional EBITDA margin cited at 13.6% vs ~16% last year. Debt in this business about Rs 50 crore; exit of consumer/B2C portion planned, institutional cleaning retained.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of around 15% reiterated on an annualised basis, though management said quarterly prediction is becoming difficult.
Management says 11.6% EBITDA margin should be the base level; steady-state EBITDA margin target of at least 15%, expected in about two years.
Pharma revenue potential of Rs 30-50 crore in the second half of FY27 (Q2/Q3 compliance target), per analyst question on the Rs 70-75 crore figure.
Finance cost guided at Rs 9-10 crore per quarter run-rate going forward (Q1 interest about Rs 11 crore).
EO supply expected by around December 2026; FY28 expected to be better with a full year of additional EO.
Saudi Arabia project: about 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products; still in survey and feedstock/land allocation stage.
capex_capacity: India capex slowed to calibrated spend; only R&D-stage new molecules (pharma, aroma chemicals) to proceed; no large spend intended this year or next.
Thailand greenfield blending plant commissioned end of Q4 FY26; investment Rs 10-15 crore; Q1 revenue about Rs 2-3 crore; currently textile products only.
EO capacity practically 100% utilised except small batch reactor addition; MDEA continuous ethoxylation plant ramp-up expected over next 12 months.
New R&D centre commissioned in Q4 FY26 and ramping up.
Andheri office sold in Q1 for about Rs 10.5 crore (other income); Kanjurmarg office sold in Q4 FY26 for about Rs 24 crore.
Saudi Arabia: initial operational and pre-operational spends only; capex not finalised.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~10% YoY; balance of growth from higher pricing.
Pass-through of raw material price increases is achieved, but frequent up/down moves create buyer uncertainty; freight and vessel availability cost margin.
Phenol loss of about Rs 5 crore in Q4 FY26 due to delayed China shipments (noted as Q1 context by management); one-off RM block purchase also hurt the quarter; prices now back to earlier levels.
Growth shifted to non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM); agro demand subdued but non-EO agro inputs grew.
Single EO supplier in India, priced on world EO price; limited negotiating power.
Freight rates rose again after brief easing; new orders taken at higher freight.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement path and timing for EBITDA margin, given flat margins over 4-5 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Sablok said 11.6% is close to last quarter and slightly below last year; margins to improve as utilisation rises, low-margin exits and pharma/aroma mix shift. Wait-and-see for at least two quarters due to pricing and RM pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is 11.6% the base margin and what is steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11.6% should be the base level. Base business ex-B2C is 14-15%; target is around 15% steady-state EBITDA margin within two years after B2C recalibration and asset monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Exit of B2C business: investment, debt and margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate investment as assets are shared (Silvassa). Debt in institutional/B2C about Rs 50 crore. Exit releases at least 2-3% EBITDA margin. Institutional cleaning retained; only consumer/B2C exits.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing vs volume growth and growth levers without EO availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~10% YoY, rest from pricing. Growth from new non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM), trace minerals, vitamin and enzyme premixes; pharma to rise to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic-focused peers gain while Rossari did not?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-molecule producers benefited; specialty players absorbed raw material hits. Phenol shipment delay from China cost about Rs 5 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi Arabia project timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Survey and feedstock/land allocation still in progress; nothing finalised. About 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest because term loans for capex were capitalised earlier and are now expensed as assets commissioned; run-rate to be Rs 9-10 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on B2C exits, asset monetisation and utilisation; management declined to guide quarterly numbers.
EO supply (single Indian supplier) expected only by about December 2026; EO-linked growth is delayed.
Raw material and freight volatility linked to West Asia/geopolitics; freight rates rose again after easing.
Thailand and Saudi Arabia ramp-up and pre-operative costs weigh on margins.
Pharma compliance timeline (Q2/Q3) gates the Rs 30-50 crore H2 revenue potential.
Interest costs rising as capitalised projects go into P&L; watch whether run-rate falls to Rs 9-10 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and long-term margins, but cautious on near-term visibility; management repeatedly said predicting quarterly results is difficult given geopolitics, freight and RM volatility. Specific on the B2C exit and margin targets, evasive on Saudi project capex and timing.
key_quotes: We commenced FY27 on a strong note, delivering our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with consolidated revenue growing 28% YoY.
Our focus as a company is to achieve EBITDA margins of 15% plus.
If you see our EO capacity now is practically 100% utilized except for a small addition in the batch reactors.
We will not stop seeding these initiatives just to show a slightly higher EBITDA margin.
